title: Diabetes emergencies in the hospital: DKA, HHS and hypoglycemia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's diabetes (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Diabetic ketoacidosis

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 36-year-old woman with a known history of type 1 diabetes who presented to the emergency department with altered mental status and signs of metabolic derangement. Laboratory testing confirmed a diagnosis of ketoacidosis secondary to several missed doses of her prescribed insulin. She was admitted to the acute care unit for stabilization. Management included aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation and the initiation of a continuous insulin drip. Her metabolic status improved steadily over the course of her stay. Her electrolyte levels and blood glucose concentrations normalized, and her acid-base balance was restored. She tolerated the treatment well and was able to transition to subcutaneous insulin prior to discharge.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Type 1 diabetes
2. Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)

Discharge Medications:
- Insulin aspart subcutaneous injections
- Potassium chloride oral solution

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with her primary care physician in one week for a review of her insulin regimen and glucose monitoring.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/15/2026
explanations: Type 1 diabetes with ketoacidosis without coma: E10.10 (HCC 36).
